---
engine: markdown
title: "Lesson 4: What Quarto adds to Markdown"
---

Everything from [Lesson 3](03-markdown.qmd) works in Quarto. This lesson covers what Quarto **adds**. None of this works on GitHub; it's Quarto only.

## 1. The YAML header

Every `.qmd` file starts with a header between two `---` lines. It's written in **YAML**: `key: value` pairs that set up the document.

```yaml
---
title: "Weekly ILI Summary"
subtitle: "Week 42, 2026"
author: "Jane Smith"
date: 2026-10-28
format: html
toc: true
---
```

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `title`, `subtitle`, `author`, `date` | Shown at the top of the output |
| `format` | The type of output: `html`, `revealjs` (slides), and others ([Lesson 6](06-documents.qmd)) |
| `toc: true` | Adds a table of contents |
| `description` | A one-line summary (used by search and link previews) |

::: {.callout-warning title="YAML is picky about spacing"}
- Put a space after the colon: `title: "Hi"`, not `title:"Hi"`.
- Indent with **spaces**, never tabs. Two spaces per level.
- Put text in quotes if it contains a colon: `title: "Lesson 1: Basics"`.
:::

## 2. Callouts

Colored boxes for notes, tips, and warnings:

```markdown
::: {.callout-note}
This is a note.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Careful"}
This deletes files.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Hidden until clicked: good for exercise answers.
:::
```

::: {.callout-note}
This is a note.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Careful"}
This deletes files.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Hidden until clicked: good for exercise answers.
:::

The five types: `callout-note`, `callout-tip`, `callout-warning`, `callout-important`, and `callout-caution`.

The `:::` lines create a **div**: a block with a name in `{ }`. Quarto uses the same pattern for tabs, columns, and more.

## 3. Tabs

Let readers choose between versions of the same content:

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows
Press **Ctrl + S**.

## Mac
Press **Cmd + S**.
:::
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows
Press **Ctrl + S**.

## Mac
Press **Cmd + S**.
:::

Add `group="os"` to several tab sets on the same site, and choosing a tab in one switches them all. The editor tabs in this training work that way.

## 4. Columns

```markdown
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
Left side
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Right side
:::

::::
```

The outer block uses **four** colons so Quarto can tell where it ends. Columns are most useful on slides ([Lesson 7](07-presentations.qmd)).

## 5. Images, captions, and alt text

```markdown
![](images/epi-curve.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of weekly measles cases, peaking at 12 in week 8."}

![Weekly measles cases, 2026](images/epi-curve.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of weekly measles cases, peaking at 12 in week 8."}
```

- **`fig-alt`** is the **alt text**: what screen-reader users hear instead of seeing the image. **Every image needs it.**
- Text in the square brackets becomes a **visible caption**. Leave them empty if you don't want one.
- Size and position: `{width="60%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="..."}`.

Good alt text says what the image shows and its main point: not "chart," but "Bar chart of weekly measles cases, peaking at 12 in week 8."

## 6. Cross-references

Give a figure an ID starting with `fig-`, and refer to it with `@`:

```markdown
![Weekly measles cases](images/epi-curve.png){#fig-measles fig-alt="..."}

Cases peaked in week 8 (@fig-measles).
```

Quarto numbers it ("Figure 1") and turns `@fig-measles` into a link. Tables use `tbl-`.

## 7. Footnotes

```markdown
Rates are per 100,000 population.^[Population estimates from the 2024 Census.]
```

Rates are per 100,000 population.^[Population estimates from the 2024 Census.]

## 8. Visual mode

All three editors have a **visual editor** that shows a `.qmd` file formatted (like a word processor), with toolbar buttons for headings, lists, tables, and callouts. It's a good way to learn the syntax: make something with the toolbar, then switch back to source to see the Markdown.

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## Positron

Right-click in the file → **Edit in Visual Mode**, or press **Ctrl + Shift + F4** (Mac: Cmd + Shift + F4). Same again to switch back.

## VS Code

Right-click in the file → **Edit in Visual Mode**, or press **Ctrl + Shift + F4** (Mac: Cmd + Shift + F4). Requires the Quarto extension.

## RStudio

Click **Visual** / **Source** at the top left of the editor.

:::

Visual mode may reformat your Markdown slightly when it saves (spacing, table layout). That's harmless.
